score_100.reason: Fig. 3A compares the likelihood of the single-neuron latent dynamical model with the PSTH baseline. The core question is whether the model captures single-trial firing variability that cannot be explained by trial averages. The graph is a box plot of log-likelihood ratios for two macaques and is worth 30 points. The likelihood-ratio definition, PSTH baseline, and normalization are central to the method and are worth 25 points. The scientific interpretation is split into two items: the model significantly outperforms the PSTH baseline in both animals, worth 25 points, and this advantage shows that single-trial firing rates systematically deviate from the trial average and can be explained by latent dynamics, worth 20 points. Point allocation: graph reproduction 30, likelihood-comparison method 25, main conclusion that the model outperforms PSTH 25, meaning of single-trial variability 20.

rubric.GT core conclusion: Fig. 3A shows that, in both macaques, the single-neuron latent dynamical model has significantly higher likelihood than the PSTH baseline computed from trial-averaged firing rates grouped by choice direction and stimulus difficulty. The log-likelihood ratio log(L_model/L_PSTH) is significantly greater than zero for both Monkey T and Monkey O, indicating that the model outperforms the trial-averaged firing rate baseline. The core conclusion is that single-trial firing rates deviate systematically from the trial average, and this deviation cannot be attributed only to Poisson point-process noise; instead, it can be captured by differences in single-trial latent decision-variable trajectories.

Scoring items.criterion: Correctly analyzes and visualizes the box plot, with log(L_model/L_PSTH) on the x-axis, two boxes corresponding to Monkey T (n=117) and Monkey O (n=67), boxes showing median, Q1-Q3, whiskers, and outliers, significance annotated for both animals, and both distributions lying above zero as in the original figure.
Scoring items.deduction_rule: Deduct the full 30 points if the panel is misidentified as a PSTH, multi-curve time series, scatter plot, or neuronal tuning-function plot. Deduct 12 points if the x-axis does not represent log(L_model/L_PSTH). Deduct 10 points if the two macaques are collapsed into one group or one box is missing. Deduct 6 points if significance annotation is missing or directionally wrong. Deduct 15 points if the result is plotted as concentrated below zero.

Scoring items.criterion: Correctly explains how model likelihood is compared with PSTH likelihood: the PSTH baseline predicts lambda(t) using trial-averaged firing rates grouped by choice direction and stimulus difficulty, the PSTH likelihood is computed as an inhomogeneous Poisson process, L_model is the normalized spike-time likelihood, the normalization is used for fair comparison with PSTH, and the comparison is performed on the same cross-validation splits.
Scoring items.deduction_rule: Deduct 10 points if the likelihood ratio is not described as comparing the model with the PSTH baseline. Deduct 8 points if the PSTH baseline is described as one global average curve rather than a condition-grouped trial average. Deduct 8 points if the normalization or fair-comparison logic is not described. Deduct 15 points if L_model/L_PSTH is misinterpreted as a firing-rate ratio or accuracy ratio.

Scoring items.criterion: Correctly states the main conclusion that the log-likelihood ratio distributions for both macaques are significantly greater than zero, demonstrating that the single-neuron latent dynamical model significantly outperforms the PSTH baseline in both animals and that this model advantage is reliable at the population level.
Scoring items.deduction_rule: Deduct 20 points if the model is claimed not to outperform PSTH or if the likelihood ratio is said to be non-significant. Deduct 8 points if only one macaque is described and the other is omitted. Deduct 10 points if only p-values or box positions are reported without explaining that the model outperforms PSTH. Deduct 8 points if significance is interpreted as a behavioral-performance difference.

Scoring items.criterion: Correctly explains the scientific meaning of the result: the model's advantage over PSTH shows that single-trial firing rates systematically deviate from their trial averages, and this variability reflects different random trajectories of the latent decision variable x(t) across trials rather than simple Poisson measurement noise.
Scoring items.deduction_rule: Deduct 10 points if the model advantage is interpreted as only improving average PSTH fitting without addressing single-trial variability. Deduct 12 points if single-trial deviation is attributed entirely to random noise. Deduct 8 points if the latent decision-variable trajectory is not mentioned. Deduct 5 points if the response overstates this panel as proving every mechanism of the model on its own.

Acceptable deviations: It is acceptable to describe log(L_model/L_PSTH) as the log-likelihood ratio or model improvement over the PSTH baseline.
It is acceptable to describe the PSTH baseline as the trial-averaged firing-rate baseline.
The exact medians and quartiles need not be reported, as long as the direction, order of magnitude, and significance are correct.
It is acceptable to describe the Wilcoxon signed-rank test as a paired non-parametric test.
It is acceptable to describe L_model normalization as removing reaction-time likelihood effects or spike-only likelihood normalization.
The sample sizes for Monkey T and Monkey O may be approximate, but they should not be reversed or off by an order of magnitude.
It is acceptable to describe single-trial variability as trial-by-trial latent trajectory variability.
rubric.Scoring instructions: High scores (85-100) require correctly reproducing the two-macaque log-likelihood-ratio box plot, explaining the comparison and normalization of L_model and L_PSTH, accurately stating that the likelihood ratio is significantly greater than zero, and explaining that this supports a single-trial latent dynamical model capturing systematic variability not explained by PSTH. Partial scores (40-84) should be assigned when the box plot and model-advantage direction are correct but the likelihood definition, normalization, or single-trial variability meaning is incomplete. Low scores (0-39) should be assigned when the panel is confused with a PSTH or behavioral-result plot, when the likelihood ratio is interpreted as a firing-rate ratio, or when the opposite conclusion that the model does not outperform PSTH is drawn.
